title: Progesterone
what: This is a blood test from a vein. From your progesterone level, the doctor can tell if you ovulated and how the second half of your cycle works.
why: When planning a pregnancy, for infertility, irregular periods, and sometimes in early pregnancy.
duration: the blood draw takes a few minutes; results usually come in 1 to 3 days
tell_doctor: How long your cycle usually is and when your last period was
If you take hormones or birth control
If you are or might be pregnant

prepare.title: Cycle day
prepare.text: Usually about 7 days before your next period is due. With a 28-day cycle, that is around day 21. Your doctor will tell you the exact day.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Best in the morning before eating, or a few hours after a light meal. Check with the lab.

prepare.title: The day before
prepare.text: For 24 hours, no alcohol and no hard workouts. Best not to smoke in the morning.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. Tell your doctor what you take. They will decide if anything should change.

bring: A record of your periods for the last few months
steps: You sit down and rest your arm on the armrest
A band is tightened above your elbow
The skin is wiped with antiseptic
A quick prick, and blood fills a tube
The needle comes out, and a cotton pad is pressed on the spot
feel: A quick prick, like a pinch
Sometimes slight dizziness. Tell the nurse
after: Press the cotton pad for 3 to 5 minutes and keep your arm straight
You can eat right away and go back to your usual day
Results usually come in 1 to 3 days. The lab will tell you when

faq.q: Why isn't progesterone tested early in the cycle?
faq.a: It rises after ovulation. So the test is done in the second half of the cycle.

faq.q: What if my cycle is irregular?
faq.a: Tell your doctor. They will suggest a day or order the test a few times.

reminders.text: Progesterone test tomorrow. Check the cycle day your doctor gave you. Best to come before eating.
